title: Host
description: M1: enrolment, the authenticated hello, and heartbeats with host facts.

x-messages.description: First and only request on an enrolment socket: trade a one-time enrol token for a host id and a long-lived credential. The panel closes with `CLOSE_ENROLLED` after answering.
First request on every run socket. Authenticates the host and replays the agent's view of its servers.
Every `heartbeatSec` seconds after a successful hello.

Replace the agent with the panel's build `sha256` and restart into it. Answers at once (`current`, or `downloading`); progress follows as `agent.updateStatus` events. The agent waits for running operations (installs, starts, stops, backups, file transfers) to finish before it restarts; game containers keep running. A newer request replaces a pending one. Agents older than M6 answer `unsupported`.
Progress of the update `agent.update` started: every state change, and `waitingFor` whenever it changes.

HostFacts.description: What the agent knows about its machine. Collected at enrol, hello and every heartbeat.

docker.description: null = Docker is not reachable on this host.

egress.description: Egress filtering for game servers. null = not checked yet (the agent is still starting) or an agent older than this field; the panel stores a missing value as null.

boundPorts.description: Host ports other software already holds, so the panel's allocator skips them (M3). null = not read (not Linux) or an agent older than this field; the panel stores a missing value as null.

agentBuild.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the running gss-agent binary, read once at start (M6). The panel compares it with the build it serves for `os.arch` to tell whether the agent is out of date. null = it could not be read; a missing value (an agent older than this field) is stored as null.

threads.description: Logical CPUs available to the agent.

DiskFacts.description: The filesystem holding the agent's data root (`/var/lib/ionnet-gss`).

EgressFacts.description: Whether the agent's nftables table (`inet ionnet_gss`) is in place. Servers without `allowPrivateNetwork` start only while it is.

filtering.description: The last apply of the table succeeded.

error.description: Why the last apply failed (e.g. the helper image is missing or `nft` refused the ruleset); null while filtering works.

checkedAt.description: When the table was last applied or the last attempt failed.

BoundPorts.description: Ports bound in the host's network namespace (`/proc/net/{tcp,tcp6,udp,udp6}`): listening TCP sockets and unconnected UDP sockets, sorted and unique, at most 4096 each. Ports Docker publishes for the agent's own servers are included (they are allocated anyway).

token.description: The one-time `gss_enrol_…` token an admin created in the panel.

credential.description: The long-lived `gss_host_…` credential. Shown once; the panel keeps only its SHA-256.

servers.description: Every server the agent manages, with its current state (M2). Empty in M1.

sha256.description: The build to install: the SHA-256 of `/api/agent/download/linux/<arch>` on the agent's own panel. The agent downloads only from its configured panel URL and refuses a file with any other digest.

force.description: Install it even if this agent rolled that build back before (`.gss-agent-rejected`). The panel sets it for a manual update, never for an automatic one. Absent = false.

AgentUpdateState.description: current: the agent already runs that build (nothing to do). downloading: fetching and verifying it. waiting: verified and staged next to the binary, waiting for `waitingFor` to finish. restarting: the binary was replaced and the agent restarts into it (it reconnects with the new `agentBuild`). failed: see `message`; the binary was not replaced.

sha256.description: The build this status is about.

message.description: One readable sentence for people (why it failed, what it waits for); may be empty.

waitingFor.description: While `waiting`: what still runs, e.g. `install of server 3f2a…`, `backup of server 3f2a…`. Empty otherwise.
